title: Efficient extraterrestrial communications would show no detectable regularities

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Efficient extraterrestrial communications would show no detectable regularities

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Signals used for communication by an advanced extraterrestrial civilization would likely be compressed to the point of showing essentially no detectable regularities, so they would look like random radio noise, and searches for sharply defined carrier frequencies would miss them; only beacons meant to be noticed would need recognizable regularities.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: my guess is that they will exhibit essentially no detectable regularities. For any such regularity represents in a sense a redundancy or inefficiency that can be removed by the sender and receiver both using appropriate data compression.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Intelligence in the Universe” (from p. 822), p. 836. Scope: extraterrestrial radio signals and searches for extraterrestrial intelligence

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-50: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public SETI observations allow method comparisons and tests on noise or simulated injections, but contain no labeled advanced communication. The central prediction therefore needs a genuine signal or other new empirical evidence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply preregistered compression and statistical-randomness tests to candidate extraterrestrial signals and compare detection sensitivity of narrowband versus structure-agnostic searches. Confirming the claim requires authenticated advanced communications; a verified communication with strong exploitable regularity would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No extraterrestrial communication has been authenticated.

Failure to detect regularity cannot prove its absence.

Compression depends on sender-receiver side information and channel constraints.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Radio surveys publicly archive astronomical emission and the results of narrowband searches. They do not contain messages identified as extraterrestrial communications, which is the variable the prediction concerns. Until such a corpus exists, a noise-like recording fits both the claim and the hypothesis that the recording is natural.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On signals independently known to be communications of a non-human technological civilization, measure repetition, spectral lines, and compressibility. Essentially no detectable regularities would support the claim for ongoing traffic; stable recognizable carriers in that traffic would refute it. Beacons meant to be noticed are excluded and scored separately.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A noise-like spectrum is the prediction both for compressed messages and for ordinary astrophysical emission.

No confirmed extraterrestrial communication corpus exists.

The beacon exception makes non-detection of carriers compatible with the claim.
